punchline: The line Murphy repeats most is "Be it done unto you as you believe", and he means it as an instruction, not a comfort.
thirty_sec: Joseph Murphy keeps returning to one verse from Matthew: "Be it done unto you as you believe." He reads it as a law: a thought held with conviction, even "I can't", becomes what you act on, so change the belief first. His support is faith and anecdotes, including a tuberculosis story he tells without medical evidence, not experiments.
